title: Etihad celebrates 115 Emirati cadet pilots and engineers at its 2026 graduation ceremony
summary: 61 Emirati cadet pilots and 54 cadet engineers graduate from Etihad’s 2025–26 programmes at the airline’s headquarters in Abu Dhabi

contentHtml:
Etihad Airways, the national airline of the UAE, today celebrates the graduation of 115 Emirati cadets from its 2025–26 programmes with a ceremony at its headquarters in Abu Dhabi. Image courtesy: Etihad Airways

61 Emirati cadet pilots and 54 cadet engineers graduate from Etihad’s 2025–26 programmes at the airline’s headquarters in Abu Dhabi

Press Release

  • More than 170 Emirati cadet pilots and almost 150 cadet engineers have graduated from Etihad’s programmes since their relaunch
  • Nearly 400 Emirati pilots now operate Etihad flights and 120 Emirati engineers and technicians maintain its fleet

ABU DHABI, UAE – Etihad Airways, the national airline of the UAE, today celebrates the graduation of 115 Emirati cadets from its 2025–26 programmes with a ceremony at its headquarters in Abu Dhabi. The graduates, 61 cadet pilots and 54 cadet engineers, were joined by their families and members of Etihad’s leadership team.

The new graduates join Etihad at a time of strong growth. The airline has doubled its fleet and will operate more than 200 aircraft by 2030. Every new aircraft and destination needs qualified pilots and engineers, and Etihad is building that capability at home through its UAE National Talent Strategy.

Antonoaldo Neves, Chief Executive Officer, Etihad Airways, said: “As Etihad continues its ambitious growth journey, Emirati talent is fundamental to our long-term success. Today’s 115 graduates show that our growth is being built by Emiratis. As we expand our fleet and network, we are investing in the pilots and engineers who will fly and maintain our aircraft for years to come.

“I congratulate every graduate on this achievement and thank their families, whose support has been with them every step of the way. We are proud to offer young Emiratis an environment where they can build meaningful careers and grow alongside the business. Their success is our success, and their journey is an inspiration to the next generation of Emiratis looking to build a career in aviation.”

Fatma Al Sahlawi, Chief People Officer, Etihad Airways, said: "Our cadet programmes attract the brightest young Emiratis and giving flight to ambition by offering them a clear path into highly skilled aviation careers. Built on a world-class syllabus and the highest international standards, with a 98% success rate, the programmes are one of the main sources of Etihad's operational talent, shaping the team that will carry the airline into its next chapter. Investing in national talent is a long-term commitment. By offering Emiratis clear career paths from cadet to the most senior roles in our operation, we are building a sustainable pipeline of national expertise that will strengthen Etihad and the UAE's aviation sector for decades to come."

The programmes are at the heart of Etihad's UAE National Talent Strategy, alongside a wider portfolio of UAE National programmes across the airline. These include the Cadet Technician Programme, launched last year, with more than 30 technicians currently in training, and the Airport Management Programme, which prepares Emiratis for airport operations and supervisory roles in Abu Dhabi and at airports across Etihad's global network. Strong demand from top performing, young Emiratis keeps intakes growing. The results are already visible across Etihad's operation: close to 400 Emirati pilots operate Etihad flights, more than one in four First Officers are Emirati, and around 120 Emirati engineers and technicians help keep its fleet flying safely.

Held during the UAE’s Year of Family, the ceremony welcomed the graduates’ families to mark the moment together. Etihad recognises the role family plays in every graduate’s journey, and the trust families place in the airline as their sons and daughters begin careers on the flight deck and in the hangar.

As the UAE’s national airline, Etihad plays a direct role in supporting the UAE’s national agenda, which makes investing in national talent a priority for the decade ahead. By empowering young Emiratis to pursue their ambitions in aviation, Etihad is helping shape a future in which national talent is central to the airline’s success and to the UAE’s continued growth.

About Etihad Airways

Etihad Airways, the national airline of the UAE, was formed in 2003 and quickly went on to become one of the world's leading airlines. From its home in Abu Dhabi, Etihad flies to passenger and cargo destinations in the Middle East, Africa, Europe, Asia, Australia, and North America. Together with Etihad's codeshare partners, Etihad's network offers access to hundreds of international destinations. In recent years, Etihad has received numerous awards for its superior service and products, cargo offering, loyalty programme and more. To learn more, visit etihad.com.
